stable_findings.remaining: Fast leader before ps and signal before list insertion leave identity unregistered; nonisolated surviving PID can cause adoption of caller PGID. Actual detached client side branch tracked separately as S2-R54-A-04.
stable_findings.smallest_closure: Establish and retain exclusively owned launch identity before client execution; unknown acquisition refuses/quarantines without adopting caller group; interrupted acquisition uses owned PID-only fallback until exclusivity proven.

stable_findings.smallest_closure: Initialize one elapsed deadline before first exceptional reap, bound final work and reserve a minimal failure receipt, derive authoritative cleanup/final truth after budgeted work.

new_findings.title: K1 shared caller group is promoted to owned cleanup set
new_findings.mechanism: Foreground-only K1 launch inherits caller PGID. Driver extracts harness PGID, enumerates entire group and excludes only itself and pattern snapshot before TERM/KILL. Unrelated caller siblings and outer N2 driver can be selected.
new_findings.smallest_closure: Exclusive identity-confirmed K1 control enclosure, preserving predecessor internals; do not adopt arbitrary log PGID. Later authorized caller-group decoy check.

new_findings.title: Stop timeout and K10 omit the hanging stop's plain child
new_findings.mechanism: Foreground stop wrapper has no owned group; sleep60 PID is not printed/recorded; name/listener census cannot certify it gone. Exact124/escalation outcome not measured.
new_findings.smallest_closure: Own stop/status client group, include bounded reap in cleanup budget, record independent stub child identity and reject any survivor.

new_findings.title: Runner changes two files after hashing them
new_findings.mechanism: SHA256SUMS includes exit-codes.txt/stamp.txt at198; both receive appended total-time text at200.
new_findings.smallest_closure: Freeze hashed files before hash; separate later receipt explicitly from inner manifest and use finite additive outer manifest ordering; gate hash/receipt errors.

new_findings.title: Actual Prisma checkpoint worker can leave owned client group
new_findings.mechanism: Prisma command dispatch invokes optional checkpoint check; unref defaults true, fork detached true, worker unrefs/disconnects. Reviewed runner and consumers do not enforce CHECKPOINT_DISABLE. Worker survival and argv not observed; names are not ownership.
new_findings.smallest_closure: Pin/stamp CHECKPOINT_DISABLE=1 for actual client graph, preserve through npx/subshells, bind dependency bytes and scoped no-detach assumption. No namespace or general hostile-process framework required by this evidence.
new_findings.dynamic_boundary: K9 NOTRUN; remains limitation observation, not ownership pass.
